clue.text: Fancy, and clever too

parts.note: to fancy something is to like it
clever means wise

explanation.surface: Someone is both imaginative and smart as well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' reads as an adjective but works as the verb meaning to be keen on.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean 'also' or 'in the same way', so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Shop that is shifting pastries first and foremost

indicators.note: says the rearranged pastries come at the very front, before the other piece
shifting the letters of the word pastries moves them into a new order

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder
i.e. is the abbreviation for 'that is' (id est)

explanation.surface: A bakery that is moving its pastries out before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shifting' rearranges PASTRIES into PATISSER; 'first and foremost' puts it ahead of IE.
explanation.definitionFit: A French-style bakery selling cakes and pastries is a type of shop.

clue.text: Die by essentially persisting with heroin

parts.note: per means by, as in 'per post'

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so the middle letters of persisting are taken

parts.note: H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A grim note that persisting with heroin will kill you.
explanation.definitionFit: To expire or lose one's life; a direct synonym for dying.

clue.text: Bird swallowing a strange green creature?

indicators.note: the bird's name takes the next piece inside it as if gulping it down

parts.note: a martin is a bird of the swallow family

explanation.surface: A bird gulps down some odd green critter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swallowing' is a sly nod, since the martin is itself a kind of swallow.
explanation.definitionFit: Little green men from Mars are the stock alien, so a strange green creature is an example.

clue.text: Small amount of saline fluid an otologist put in a cap

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other, here the doctor goes into the cap

parts.note: a cap or lid is a top
an otologist is an ear doctor, EAR plus DR

explanation.surface: An ear specialist administers a little saline solution into a cap.
explanation.definitionFit: Tears are salty, so a single tear is a tiny quantity of salty liquid.

clue.text: Save time for the end

parts.note: save in the sense 'except' means but

explanation.surface: Keep some time in reserve for the finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Save' looks like a verb; it is the preposition meaning except.
explanation.definitionFit: A butt is the thicker or remaining end of something, like a cigarette or rifle.

clue.text: Hot Christmas cake left out

indicators.note: out says a letter is dropped from the cake's name

parts.note: stollen is a German fruit loaf eaten at Christmas

explanation.surface: A Christmas cake left sitting out somewhere warm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot' reads as temperature but is slang for stolen goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot is slang for goods obtained by theft, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Rant coming from one stuck in traffic

indicators.note: one piece is lodged inside the other word

parts.note: to traffic is to trade, especially illicitly
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A furious outburst from a driver caught in a jam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'traffic' suggests cars, but here means commerce.
explanation.definitionFit: A long angry speech is a rant; the words are synonyms.

clue.text: Acceptable way to correspond after a date

indicators.note: the correspondence word follows the other two pieces in the answer

parts.note: to equate is to make things correspond or match

explanation.surface: A suitable way of keeping in touch following a date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'correspond' suggests letters, but here means to match.
explanation.definitionFit: Something satisfactory or good enough is passable, which is the sense of the answer.

clue.text: Female artist is in Germany advocating for women's rights

parts.note: Tracey Emin is a British artist
ist is German for 'is'

explanation.surface: A woman artist living in Germany campaigns for equality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is in Germany' looks like a location but gives the German word for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Campaigning for women's equality is the core of the movement, so the adjective fits.

clue.text: Toy snake missing its tail

indicators.note: the snake loses its last letter

parts.note: rattler is a name for a rattlesnake

explanation.surface: A toy snake that has lost its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: The snake is a rattlesnake, whose tail is the very part that rattles.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby's noisemaker that shakes is a classic plaything.

clue.text: Equipment given to school is trash

parts.note: kit is equipment or gear

explanation.surface: Gear donated to a school turns out to be rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasteless, tacky art or objects are dismissed as rubbish; kitsch names that quality.

clue.text: I'm overwhelmed by a friend's ill-will

indicators.note: the first pieces are surrounded and swamped by the following pieces

parts.note: a crony is a close friend; the apostrophe s links to the definition
taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Someone is hurt by the hostility of a pal.
explanation.definitionFit: Bitter hostility or resentment is a synonym of ill-will.

clue.text: Influential teacher's remit soon involved taking the end of classes

definitions.note: the apostrophe s is 'is', linking definition to wordplay

indicators.note: involved means intricately tangled, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

indicators.note: the last letter of classes is taken

explanation.surface: An educator's brief is soon taking in final lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges REMITSOON plus S, the last letter from 'the end of' classes.
explanation.definitionFit: Maria Montessori was an Italian educator whose child-centred method is used worldwide.

clue.text: Something great in a fishing boat

definitions.meaning: Australian slang for a real beauty or something excellent
a vessel used for diving or fishing for pearls

explanation.surface: Something wonderful found aboard a trawler.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an Australian term for something first-rate and a boat used in pearl fishing.

clue.text: I soon made up with them, with no hard feelings

indicators.note: made up means put together anew, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

indicators.note: the letter for hard is dropped from them

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: I'll soon reconcile with them, with no hard feelings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no' drops H from THEM, leaving TEM; 'made up' rearranges ISOON plus TEM.
explanation.definitionFit: Feelings such as joy and anger are emotional states; a synonym in the plural.

clue.text: Dog lies barking, guarding a bowl

indicators.note: the anagram surrounds the bowl as if protecting it
barking means mad, so the letters go wild

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder
a pan is a shallow bowl or dish

explanation.surface: A dog lying down barks while defending its food bowl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barking' (mad) rearranges the fodder into SIEL; 'lies' looks like resting but is only letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The spaniel is a breed of gundog with long ears.

clue.text: Bloated? Stop drinking dodgy lager!

indicators.note: the stop word takes the anagram inside it as if swallowing it

parts.note: to stop is to end

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Feeling bloated? Then give up the bad lager!
explanation.definitionFit: Swollen or made bigger, as a bloated belly is expanded.

clue.text: Salesman is very critical about fish

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the pieces read backwards

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
to pan a play is to criticise it harshly

explanation.surface: A salesman harshly critiques some fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The red snapper is a familiar sea fish, an example of the category.

clue.text: Stressed vehicle owner crashed

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: a crash smashes things up, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: An anxious motorist has crashed.
explanation.definitionFit: Showing the strain of worry and hardship; worn down by cares.

clue.text: Advert in a Latvian city about one in Morocco

indicators.note: the advert goes inside the turned city
about means turned round, so the city is read backwards

parts.note: Riga is the capital of Latvia

explanation.surface: An advert in Riga concerning a Moroccan town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns the city to AGIR; 'about' could pass for 'concerning', but it is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Agadir is a resort port on Morocco's Atlantic coast, so it is one Moroccan city.

clue.text: Woman dances around with no top on

indicators.note: around means turned back, so the remaining letters read backwards
the first letter of the dances word is dropped, as the top of a down entry

parts.note: ballets are dances

explanation.surface: A woman dances topless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no top on' drops B from BALLETS, and 'around' reverses ALLETS.
explanation.definitionFit: Stella is a female first name, so it is a woman's name.

clue.text: Hustler almost confused a private detective

indicators.note: confused means mixed up, so the letters are rearranged
the last letter of the word hustler is dropped

explanation.surface: A con man nearly bamboozled a private eye.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleuth is an informal word for an investigator or private eye.

clue.text: Cloth garment a fellow wears for a hunting expedition

indicators.note: the garment goes around the other pieces, as clothing covers its wearer

parts.note: a sari is a draped cloth garment worn in South Asia

explanation.surface: A man dons a cloth garment for a hunting trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wears' runs backwards: here the garment holds the man, not the reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: A safari is an overland trip in Africa to hunt or watch big game.

clue.text: A tipple from East Italy? Quite the opposite!

indicators.note: the letters are taken out from within the words East Italy

explanation.surface: A drink from eastern Italy? No, the reverse!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quite the opposite!' is a joke: the wine comes from Piedmont in north-west Italy, not the east.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a sparkling Italian wine, so it is an alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Request user-generated content

parts.note: a plea is an earnest request

indicators.note: generated means produced afresh, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: A call for material created by users online.
explanation.walkthrough: 'content' reads as web material but is the adjective-turned-noun sense of satisfaction.
explanation.definitionFit: Content as a noun means contentment or satisfaction, a synonym of enjoyment.

clue.text: A little bit of bread, occasionally nice with topping of Emmental

parts.note: pitta is a flat bread

indicators.note: occasionally means every so often, so alternate letters of nice are taken
the top, first letter of Emmental is taken

explanation.surface: A small piece of bread, sometimes pleasant with cheese on top.
explanation.definitionFit: A pittance is a very small amount, especially of money.

clue.text: Politicians love blocking judges

indicators.note: the love letter sits inside the judges word, blocking it

parts.note: to try a case is to judge it
love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: Politicians who are fond of obstructing the judiciary.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of Britain's Conservative Party are Tories, a group of politicians.
